keywords.def: increasing without any attempt to limit or prevent it
eat grass (animal); continually eat small bites of food (person)
situation in which an animal or plant species no longer exists
situation in which wild animals are controlled by humans for work, food or as pets
very eager for something, especially food

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. Neil, do you remember the children's television show, Lassie?
sentences.zh: 我是 Neil。我是 Beth。Neil，你还记得那部儿童电视剧《灵犬莱西》(Lassie)吗？

sentences.en: Oh yes, of course. The show's hero was a dog named Lassie.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然记得。剧中的主角是一只名叫 Lassie 的狗。

sentences.en: And Lassie went round helping people in trouble.
sentences.zh: Lassie 到处帮助遇到麻烦的人。

sentences.en: Yes. Well, if you watched Lassie as a child, you might also remember the TV shows, Flipper the Dolphin, and Skippy the Kangaroo.
sentences.zh: 没错。如果你小时候看过《灵犬莱西》，可能还记得《海豚飞宝》(Flipper the Dolphin)和《袋鼠史奇比》(Skippy the Kangaroo)这两部电视剧。

sentences.en: The stars of these shows were animals who would also come to the rescue of humans in trouble.
sentences.zh: 这些剧的主角都是动物，它们同样会在人类遇到麻烦时挺身相救。

sentences.en: In this programme, we'll be discussing some real-life animals helping people in trouble.
sentences.zh: 在这期节目中，我们要聊聊现实生活中帮助人类脱险的动物。

sentences.en: It might sound strange, but we'll be hearing how cows are helping to stop fires in Spain!
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能有点奇怪，但我们要讲的是，奶牛是如何帮忙在西班牙扑灭火灾的！

sentences.en: Well, now I have a picture in my head of a cow wearing a fireman's helmet, but I guess that's not what you mean, Neil.
sentences.zh: 这下我脑海里浮现出一头戴着消防员头盔的奶牛，不过我猜这不是你的意思吧，Neil。

sentences.en: Not quite, Beth, but you're right about the fires, or wildfires to be exact.
sentences.zh: 不完全是，Beth，不过你说的火灾没错，准确来说是野火(wildfires)。

sentences.en: Wildfires are unplanned fires, in areas like forests or grasslands, which spread out of control.
sentences.zh: 野火是指在森林或草原等地区意外发生、并且失控蔓延的火灾。

sentences.en: They often happen in hot dry countries like Spain.
sentences.zh: 这种火灾常常发生在像西班牙这样炎热干燥的国家。

sentences.en: So, how could cows help? We'll be finding out and learning some useful new vocabulary as well.
sentences.zh: 那么，奶牛究竟能帮上什么忙呢？我们马上就会揭晓答案，同时也会学到一些实用的新词汇。

sentences.en: And remember, if you like to read along as you listen to the programme, you'll find a script on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，如果你想边听节目边看文字稿，可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到。

sentences.en: But now I have a question for you, Beth.
sentences.zh: 现在我有个问题要考考你，Beth。

sentences.en: Some wildfires are caused naturally, but most are the result of human activity.
sentences.zh: 有些野火是自然引发的，但大多数其实是人类活动造成的。

sentences.en: So, according to the Natural History Museum of Utah, what proportion of wildfires is caused by people?
sentences.zh: 那么，根据犹他州自然历史博物馆的数据，野火中有多大比例是由人为原因引起的？

sentences.en: Is it: a) two out of every five b) three out of every five c) four out of every five I'm going to guess three out of every five, I think.
sentences.zh: 是 a) 五分之二？b) 五分之三？还是 c) 五分之四？我想我猜五分之三。

sentences.en: Let's find out at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 我们节目最后揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Thanks to increasing temperatures caused by climate change, the wildfires happening today are more intense and more destructive than ever before.
sentences.zh: 由于气候变化导致气温上升，如今的野火比以往任何时候都更加猛烈、破坏力也更强。

sentences.en: Here, Craig Langran, reporter for BBC World Service programme, People Fixing the World, discusses the problem with Pablo Schapira, of Rewilding Spain, an organisation combating wildfires in central Spain:
sentences.zh: 下面是 BBC 世界服务频道节目《People Fixing the World》记者 Craig Langran，与致力于在西班牙中部对抗野火的组织 Rewilding Spain 的 Pablo Schapira 就这一问题展开的讨论：

sentences.en: One of the reasons for this is that the forests have been left to grow unchecked as there simply aren't enough animals to feed on all the trees, bushes and grass.
sentences.zh: 原因之一是森林一直处于无人控制的疯长状态(left to grow unchecked)，因为已经没有足够多的动物来啃食这些树木、灌木和青草了。

sentences.en: And the more dense this vegetation is, the more likely it is to catch fire.
sentences.zh: 而植被越茂密，就越容易起火。

sentences.en: What we had before in our ecosystems here in Europe is that we had big grazers: we had bison, we had tauros, we had wild horses.
sentences.zh: 以前我们欧洲的生态系统里曾经有大型食草动物：比如野牛、原牛(tauros)和野马。

sentences.en: And now they are gone from the ecosystem because of extinction, domestication.
sentences.zh: 而如今，由于灭绝和驯化，它们已经从生态系统中消失了。

sentences.en: Many European forests have grown unchecked.
sentences.zh: 许多欧洲森林一直处于失控疯长的状态。

sentences.en: If something is left unchecked, nobody controls it or prevents it from increasing.
sentences.zh: 如果某样东西被 left unchecked(放任不管)，就是说没有人控制它或阻止它继续增长。

sentences.en: The problem is that when trees, grass and vegetation are left to grow, they're more likely to catch fire.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，树木、青草和植被一旦被放任生长，就更容易起火。

sentences.en: Hundreds of years ago, animals known as grazers would simply have eaten this vegetation up.
sentences.zh: 几百年前，那些被称为食草动物(grazers)的动物本会把这些植被吃掉。

sentences.en: To graze means to eat grass and other wild plants, and grazers are the animals, including horses, cows and goats, which do this.
sentences.zh: graze 意思是吃草和其他野生植物，grazers 则是指做这件事的动物，包括马、牛和山羊。

sentences.en: In English, you can also say a person is grazing if they continually eat snacks or little bites of food.
sentences.zh: 在英语里，如果一个人不停地吃零食或一小口一小口地吃东西，也可以说他在 grazing。

sentences.en: But in modern times, numbers of grazing animals have declined sharply because of extinction, when a species of animal – the dinosaurs for example – no longer exist, and domestication, when wild animals are controlled by humans to work or for food.
sentences.zh: 但在现代，食草动物的数量因为灭绝(extinction，即某个物种彻底消失，比如恐龙)和驯化(domestication，即野生动物被人类控制用来劳作或食用)而大幅减少。

sentences.en: And as numbers of grazing wild animals decrease, forest and grasslands continue to grow unchecked, leading to the large wildfires which now regularly happen in Spain.
sentences.zh: 随着野生食草动物数量减少，森林和草原持续失控生长，这也导致了如今在西班牙频繁发生的大规模野火。

sentences.en: And that's where our four-legged friends, the cows, come to the rescue.
sentences.zh: 而这时候，我们的四条腿朋友——奶牛，就来救场了。

sentences.en: Supported by Rewilding Spain, Pablo has reintroduced herds of tauros – the species of cow similar to the now-extinct wild aurochs, the ancestor of the modern domestic cow – into the forests of central Spain.
sentences.zh: 在 Rewilding Spain 的支持下，Pablo 将成群的原牛(tauros)重新引入了西班牙中部的森林——这是一种与如今已灭绝的野生原牛(现代家牛的祖先)相似的牛种。

sentences.en: Here's reporter, Craig Langran, again for BBC World Service programme, People Fixing the World:
sentences.zh: 下面再次是 BBC 世界服务频道节目《People Fixing the World》记者 Craig Langran 的报道：

sentences.en: Along with the cows' voracious appetite, they trample on the vegetation, and it's that trampling that helps to open up the forest so it's not so densely packed full of flammable vegetation.
sentences.zh: 这些牛不仅食欲旺盛，还会踩踏植被，正是这种踩踏(trampling)有助于让森林变得疏朗，不再挤满易燃的植被。

sentences.en: Tauros eat everything from grass and leaves to tree branches and bark, each consuming over 30 kilos a day.
sentences.zh: 原牛几乎什么都吃，从青草、树叶到树枝、树皮，每头牛每天要吃掉 30 多公斤。

sentences.en: Craig says the cows are voracious, or very eager for lots of food.
sentences.zh: Craig 说这些牛食欲旺盛(voracious)，也就是非常渴望大量进食。

sentences.en: What's more, by wandering freely around the forest they trample down dead trees, reducing the amount of flammable, meaning easily burned, vegetation.
sentences.zh: 此外，它们在森林里自由漫步的同时，还会踩倒枯树，从而减少易燃(flammable，即容易着火)的植被数量。

sentences.en: They don't wear firemen's helmets, but these four-legged, fire-fighting friends are really coming to the rescue in Spain.
sentences.zh: 它们虽然不戴消防员头盔，但这些四条腿的'消防员'朋友，确实正在西班牙发挥着救援的作用。

sentences.en: OK. Neil, isn't it time to reveal the answer to your question?
sentences.zh: 好了，Neil，是不是该公布你那个问题的答案了？

sentences.en: Yes. I asked you, What proportion of wildfires are caused by people?
sentences.zh: 对。我问你的是，野火中有多大比例是人为造成的？

sentences.en: And I said, "Three out of five." Was I right?
sentences.zh: 我说的是'五分之三'。我猜对了吗？

sentences.en: I'm afraid you're wrong, Beth. The answer was c).
sentences.zh: 恐怕你猜错了，Beth。正确答案是 c)。

sentences.en: According to the Natural History Museum of Utah, four out of every five wildfires are manmade.
sentences.zh: 根据犹他州自然历史博物馆的数据，每五场野火中就有四场是人为造成的。

sentences.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned from this programme, starting with the adjective unchecked.
sentences.zh: 好，我们来回顾一下这期节目学到的词汇，先从形容词 unchecked 开始。

sentences.en: If something harmful is left unchecked, nobody controls it or prevents it from growing.
sentences.zh: 如果某种有害的东西被 left unchecked(放任不管)，就是说没有人控制它或阻止它继续扩大。

sentences.en: To graze means to eat grass and vegetation.
sentences.zh: graze 意思是吃草和植被。

sentences.en: G razers are animals, like cows, which do this, and a person who grazes continually eats little bites of food.
sentences.zh: grazers 指的是像牛这样以此为食的动物，而一个 grazes(不停小口进食)的人，则是指不停吃零食的人。

sentences.en: Extinction is when an animal species no longer exists.
sentences.zh: extinction(灭绝)是指某个动物物种不复存在。

sentences.en: The dinosaurs and the wild aurochs are two examples of extinct animals.
sentences.zh: 恐龙和野生原牛就是两个已灭绝动物的例子。

sentences.en: Domestication is when wild animals become controlled by humans for work, food or as pets.
sentences.zh: domestication(驯化)是指野生动物被人类控制，用来劳作、食用或作为宠物。

sentences.en: The adjective voracious means very eager for something, especially a lot of food.
sentences.zh: 形容词 voracious 意思是极度渴望某样东西，尤其是大量的食物。

sentences.en: And finally, if something is flammable,iteasily burns or catches fire.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果某样东西是 flammable(易燃的)，就是说它很容易燃烧或着火。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. If you enjoyed this programme, why not check out the accompanying worksheet and quiz, both available at bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 六分钟又到了。如果你喜欢这期节目，不妨去看看配套的练习题和小测验，两者都可以在 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到。

sentences.en: Goodbye! Goodbye for now.
sentences.zh: 再见！先说再见啦。
